keyFindings.text: **`lookup()` stays synchronous and unchanged; a new exported async `lookupWithFallback()` is the seam.** `lookup()` is exported and directly asserted by the test suite, so changing its signature or making it async would break callers. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/trigger-index.vitest.ts:33-35] The wrapper calls `lookup()` with `limit: 0`, decides on the scored-hit path, and applies the slice itself. `lookup()` already builds the full ordered list before slicing, so `limit: 0` costs no extra scoring. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:238-239] `main()` becomes async and the `isMainModule` block assigns the resolved code. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:382-384]

**Answer field: `staleFallback`, present only when the fallback ran.** Shape: `{ available, files, matches, paths, truncated }`. `available` is false outside a work tree or without git; `files` counts candidate `.md` files examined; `matches` counts documents merged; `paths` lists the merged paths sorted; `truncated` is true when the candidate list exceeded the cap. Assigning it after `lookup()` appends it last in the serialized object, so the common-path JSON stays byte-identical.

**Candidate source: `git status --porcelain=v1 -z --untracked-files=all -- <roots>`.** `-z` removes quoting and makes rename records unambiguous. `--untracked-files=all` is required: the default `normal` mode collapses a wholly untracked packet directory to one `dir/` entry, so a newly created, never-`git add`ed packet would be invisible to the fallback — the exact case the fallback exists to cover. [INFERENCE: based on git status porcelain's documented default untracked mode, which reports an untracked directory as a single entry] Phase 2 measured the non-`-z` form at `0.88-0.90s` repo-wide and `0.02-0.03s` packet-scoped. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/028-sweet-search-integration/002-retrieval-lessons-research/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:30] `git ls-files --modified --others` stays rejected: it lost 14 of 29 changed docs, all staged additions. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/028-sweet-search-integration/002-retrieval-lessons-research/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:32]

**Compatibility is clean on the production side.** `generate-trigger-index.mjs` imports only `loadIndex`, and `core/workflow.ts` imports only `loadIndex` from the lookup module. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:62] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/core/workflow.ts:286-300] No production consumer parses the lookup answer; only the CLI and the test suite do.

**Contract amendments are two short blocks in sections 4 and 5** (exact wording below), because the current section 5 promise covers "two runs over an unchanged corpus" without qualifying worktree state. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/retrieval/retrieval-conventions.md:212]

**Exit rules.** Exit `0` when any merged result scores above zero; exit `1` only when the index and the fallback both produced nothing; exit `2` unchanged for bad invocation or an unreadable index. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:379]

**Module boundary: a new `lib/changed-docs.mjs`, imported dynamically only on a zero-hit.** The lookup header states that the import list is deliberately short because every extra module is paid for on every cold lookup. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:9-15] A static import of a module that itself imports the shared frontmatter parser would charge every hit for a fallback that never runs. A dynamic `await import('./lib/changed-docs.mjs')` inside the zero-hit branch pays only when the fallback fires.

**Opt-out: `--no-stale-fallback`, plus the implicit `--index` opt-out.** The flag restores index-only behavior on the default index path for parity harnesses and determinism tests. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/028-sweet-search-integration/002-retrieval-lessons-research/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:49]

**Parsing rules for `--porcelain=v1 -z`.** Each ordinary entry is `XY <path>\0`. A rename or copy (`R`/`C` in either status column) emits `XY <new-path>\0<old-path>\0`, so the parser must consume a second field and keep the new path. Deletions (`D`) name a file that no longer exists and are skipped. Submodule changes and any directory entry are excluded by the `*.md` suffix plus an `fs.statSync(...).isFile()` check. Staged additions (`A `) are kept — the case `ls-files` lost.

**Performance budget.** Scoped: git `0.02-0.03s` plus frontmatter read/score `0.02s`, below the lookup's own `0.07s`. Repo-wide: `0.88-0.90s`, roughly thirteen times the lookup it rescues. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/028-sweet-search-integration/002-retrieval-lessons-research/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:30] The zero-hit-only gate is the primary bound; a `MAX_FALLBACK_FILES = 200` cap over the sorted candidate list bounds the pathological worktree and reports `truncated: true`.

**Root and scope: the fallback belongs to the caller's work tree, not to an explicit index artifact.** The root comes from `callerRepoRoot()`, which already returns `null` for a missing git binary, a directory outside a checkout, or any git failure. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/host-index.mjs:47-56] `--spec-folder` becomes the git pathspec, and `specFolderMatches` is re-applied after parsing as a belt-and-braces filter. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:136-140] **An explicit `--index` disables the fallback**: a temp or parity artifact is by definition index-only, and this resolves phase 2's determinism tension while keeping every existing fixture hermetic. [SOURCE: specs/hooks-plugins-extensions/028-sweet-search-integration/002-retrieval-lessons-research/research/iterations/iteration-001.md:36]

**Scoring: `readTriggerPhrases` → normalized phrases → `scorePhrase`, best-per-document.** `readTriggerPhrases` returns `phrases: [{ line, normalized, raw, truncated }]` plus one category, so malformed and missing-frontmatter documents simply yield no phrases and are skipped. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/frontmatter.mjs:284-294] Each normalized phrase is scored with `scorePhrase(normalizedQuery, normalizedPhrase)`; every non-null score is above zero (`0.60`–`1.00`), so no zero-score rows can enter. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/normalize.mjs:129-151] The best score per document wins, with the existing `matchClassRank` tie-break mirroring the index loop. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs:205-223] Candidate paths are sorted with `compareCodeUnits` before reading, so file-read order and output order never depend on git's output order. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lib/normalize.mjs:172-176]
**The test matrix is the bulk of the work**, not the code: staged addition, untracked directory, rename, deletion, non-git, missing git binary, cap, determinism, and the existing fixture isolation.

**`structuredCappedRecipe` has zero callers anywhere in the repository.** Its only code occurrence is the definition; the wrapper's structured builder is uncapped, and `assertRecipeParity` compares the wrapper against the uncapped lane builder only. keyFindings.text: **A body line class demotes that wall generically, but it cannot separate the rows inside it.** All 783 blockquote rows would receive the same `guidance` class, so ordering among them still falls to path and line. The visible change is that the one prose row in the set rises above them; it does not make the flood smaller or more informative. This is the key correction to the phase 2 framing: the flood is a volume problem, which feature 3's per-file cap owns, not a class problem. [INFERENCE: applying the proposed three-class rule to the 787-row measurement in Finding 1]

keyFindings.text: **Demoting template folders gets almost none of the free-text value and belongs to the other lane.** Of the 786 stock-sentence paths, 783 are real packets that copied the template sentence and only 3 are under `templates/examples` — 0.4% of the free-text result set. The template problem that *is* measured is on the keyed lane: `acceptance criteria closure gate` still returns the three level-2, level-3 and level-3+ acceptance-criteria template copies at `query-containment` 0.88 in slots 3-5 of 6, ahead of a real packet at `token-overlap` 0.75. [INFERENCE: keyed lookup run this iteration; ranking shape at .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/lookup-trigger-index.mjs] That inversion cannot be fixed by a path tie-break placed after score; it needs either the judge's `template-default` class persisted in the artifact (schema 2 to 3) or a policy that demotes template documents ahead of score — and that policy would also demote a legitimate search for the template itself. It is a separate decision, not part of this feature.
